name: Shem
overview: Shem was a male descendant of Noah, known primarily as one of Noah's three sons who survived the Flood. He is notably recognized as the father of several significant descendants, and his lineage plays a crucial role in biblical history. There are no additional tribal or surname details recorded for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shem means 'name' or 'fame' and is recorded as a proper name in Genesis 5:32. This name was not given by God but reflects his identity as noted in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Shem is identified as the son of Noah and the father of Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram, establishing his role as a patriarch in the biblical genealogies. These relationships are inferred from Genesis 5:32 and Genesis 10:22.
scriptureSignificance: Shem's importance lies in his position as the ancestor of the Semitic peoples, including the line that leads to Abraham and ultimately the Messiah. He was present during the Flood on the ark and was part of the family that respectfully cared for Noah after the Flood. His long life allowed him to witness multiple generations of his descendants, underscoring his foundational role in God's covenantal plan.
